annual_report.name: Annual Report
annual_report.due: between January 1 and June 30 each year (starting the year after formation)
annual_report.late_penalty: administrative dissolution if not filed; $100 reinstatement penalty

state_tax_on_llc.name: Limited Liability Entity Tax (LLET)
state_tax_on_llc.applies: every business with liability protection under state law: LLCs (incl. single-member), S corporations, corporations, limited partnerships; not sole proprietorships or general partnerships
state_tax_on_llc.notes: $175 minimum if Kentucky gross receipts or gross profits are $3 million or less; above $6 million: 0.095% of Kentucky gross receipts or 0.75% of Kentucky gross profits (lesser); sliding scale between $3M and $6M

sources.title: Kentucky SOS - Fees
sources.quote: Limited Liability Company (Profit, Non-Profit or Professional Service) Articles of Organization: $40.00

sources.title: Kentucky DOR - Corporation Income and Limited Liability Entity Tax
sources.quote: If either total gross receipts or total gross profits amounts to $3 million or less, then the company just pays a $175 minimum LLET.

sources.title: Kentucky SOS - Annual Reports
sources.quote: Reports can be filed any time between January 1 and June 30 ... accompanied by a $15 filin[g fee]

entity_level_taxes.name: Limited Liability Entity Tax (LLET)
entity_level_taxes.notes: $175 minimum up to $3M gross receipts/profits; 0.095% of gross receipts or 0.75% of gross profits above $6M

pte_elective_tax.rate_note: Elective pass-through entity tax enacted in 2023 (Form 740-PTET); owners receive a refundable PTE tax credit. Rate presumably the individual rate (3.5% for 2026) - not read on an official page.

sources.title: Kentucky DOR - LLET
sources.quote: This includes corporations, LLCs, S-Corporations, limited partnerships, and other types of businesses.

sources.title: Kentucky DOR - New Pass-through Entity Tax Forms Available
sources.quote: The new Form 740-PTET allows for the election to pay the tax at the entity level

personal_exemption.notes: No personal exemption deduction (family size tax credit for low incomes, not verified). Standard deduction $3,360 per return for 2026; MFJ left null: whether a joint return gets one or two $3,360 deductions (spouses may file separately on a combined return, each claiming one) was not verified. 2027 standard deduction $3,470.

income_tax_2026.surtaxes: None at state level; local occupational license taxes apply (see local_taxes). Rate cut from 4% (2025) to 3.5% (2026).

sources.title: Kentucky DOR - Employer Payroll Withholding
sources.quote: The Kentucky Withholding Tax rate will be 3.5% for tax year 2026.

sources.title: Kentucky DOR Announces 2026 Standard Deduction (Sept 4, 2025)
sources.quote: After adjusting for inflation, the standard deduction for 2026 is $3,360, an increase of $90.

estimated_tax.notes: Form 740-ES; threshold (commonly $500) and dates not read on an official page today

unemployment_2026.notes: kcc.ky.gov (Office of Unemployment Insurance) returned 403 today

local_taxes.name: Occupational license tax on wages and net profits (Metro + school board + TARC)
local_taxes.applies: net profits of businesses and self-employed individuals operating in Louisville Metro, and wages earned there
local_taxes.threshold_or_exemption: Rate not verified: louisvilleky.gov blocked (Cloudflare 403). Commonly published total 2.20% for residents and 1.45% for nonresidents - unverified.

local_taxes.name: Occupational license fee
local_taxes.applies: individual compensation and business net profits earned in Lexington-Fayette County
local_taxes.threshold_or_exemption: plus school board tax on some items not verified
local_taxes.quote: LFUCG assesses a 2.25% occupational license fee on individual compensation and net profits.

local_taxes.place: Many other Kentucky cities and counties
local_taxes.name: Local occupational license taxes on net profits/wages
local_taxes.applies: net profits and wages, rates set locally (commonly about 1%-2.5%)
local_taxes.threshold_or_exemption: No official consolidated list was read today

notable: Even a single-member LLC owes the $175 minimum LLET each year, on top of the $15 annual report (https://revenue.ky.gov/Business/Corporation-Income-and-Limited-Liability-Entity-Tax/Pages/default.aspx)
Cities and counties levy occupational license taxes on net profits, e.g. Lexington 2.25% (https://www.lexingtonky.gov/departments/revenue)
